property_summary: For every caller address that is the admin, calling setOwner(x) updates the public owner getter to x on the reference contract; the mutant that omits the assignment will leave owner unchanged and thus violate this rule for some fuzzed owner address.

For any address supplied to setOwner by the admin, the reference contract sets owner to that supplied address; the mutant instead sets owner to address(0) and thus will differ for any input where the supplied address is not address(0).

For all callers, only the contract's original admin (the deployer) can successfully call setOwner; the mutant allowing owner to call setOwner lets a non-admin owner change owner and thus violates this invariant for some inputs (when owner != admin).

Invariant: Only the deployer (admin) can successfully call setOwner; thus for any caller address x, if x != deployer then calling setOwner(x) does not change c.owner() (reference enforces admin-only), but the mutant (which checks owner instead of admin) allows a call by current owner to change owner when owner != admin, violating this invariant for some fuzzed inputs.

For every caller A and newOwner N, only the original deployer (admin) can successfully change owner via setOwner(N); the mutant lets the current owner (when different from admin) change owner, so there exist A,N where a call that should fail in the reference instead succeeds in the mutant and c.owner() differs.

For any caller addrCaller and candidate newOwner, only the original deployer (admin) is able to successfully change c.owner() via setOwner; the mutant that checks msg.sender == owner instead of admin allows the current owner (when different from admin) to change owner, so there exist fuzzed inputs where a caller that is the current owner (but not the admin) can change the owner in the mutant but not in the reference.
For every call to setOwner by the admin that completes, the reference contract always returns true; the mutant returns false for some such calls, breaking this return-value guarantee.

For every call to setOwner by the admin, the reference contract always returns true (call completes and returns true); the mutant can return false for some inputs because it returns (owner != _owner) after assignment.

For any caller address, if C.setOwner(...) succeeds (does not revert) when called by the contract's admin, it always returns true; the mutant that zeroes admin inside the onlyAdmin modifier can cause subsequent calls to behave differently, letting a call sequence exist where reference returns true for every successful setOwner but the mutant can make an identical call sequence produce a different observable result (a later call by the previous admin will fail/return false or revert).
